statements.impact_statement: CVE-2026-50162 (GO-2026-5879, GHSA-8xwf-rjm4-xvhv): the oras-go file content store, package oras.land/oras-go/v2/content/file, confines writes to its working directory with a lexical path check only, so a pushed blob whose title passes through a symlink inside the working directory can be written outside it. It is fixed in oras-go 2.6.1. The Go vulnerability database lists file.New and Store.Add as the affected symbols, and the fix commit adds a symlink check to (*Store).resolveWritePath in content/file/file.go. Sources: https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-5879, https://github.com/oras-project/oras-go/security/advisories/GHSA-8xwf-rjm4-xvhv, https://github.com/oras-project/oras-go/commit/cc323e564d90c6b5b4bdd71d3c8d2ee2713b37e5 . We checked every published trivy-dev package for Alpine 3.23 in the DHI Alpine repository: 38 builds, 0.69.1-r0 to the current 0.74.0-r12, each for x86_64 and aarch64, each verified against the repository index checksum. Each package holds one file, /usr/bin/trivy, a statically linked Go program built with CGO_ENABLED=0. We read its Go build information (go version -m) and its function table (go tool nm), and searched its raw bytes, which also finds the names of inlined functions. The Go build information lists oras.land/oras-go/v2 2.6.0 in builds before 0.71.2-r1, inside the affected range, 2.6.1 in 0.71.2-r1 and 0.71.2-r2, and 2.6.2 from 0.71.2-r3 on. trivy links other oras-go packages, such as the registry/remote client and its auth and credentials packages, but in every build the function table has no function of package oras.land/oras-go/v2/content/file, so neither file.New, (*Store).Add, (*Store).Push, (*Store).pushFile nor (*Store).resolveWritePath is present, while runtime.main is. The raw-byte search of every build finds no oras-go content/file name or source path, and no resolveWritePath, (*Store).pushFile, (*Store).Add or content/file.New string. As a positive control, the same function-table and byte searches on a program built against oras-go 2.6.0 that calls file.New, (*Store).Add and (*Store).Push find (*Store).Add, (*Store).Push, (*Store).pushFile and (*Store).resolveWritePath, and file.New when built without inlining. The control programs were built with Go 1.27.1, CGO_ENABLED=0, for linux/amd64 and linux/arm64. The vulnerable code is not in the shipped binary.
